chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abdillah, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali, from Abu al-Hasan, Sahib al-'Askar, عليه السلام, who said:

The Greatest Name of Allah is seventy-three letters. One letter was with Asif, so he spoke by it, and the earth was split open for him through what was between him and Saba; then he took the throne of Bilqis until he brought it to Sulayman. Then the earth spread back in less than the blink of an eye. And with us, of it, are seventy-two letters, while one letter is with Allah, exclusively reserved by Him in the knowledge of the unseen.

key_terms.آصَفَ: Asif, the figure who possessed one letter of the Greatest Name and used it for a miraculous act.
key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ الْأَعْظَمُ: The Greatest Name of Allah, associated here with extraordinary divine power and knowledge.
key_terms.سَبَإٍ: Saba, the land associated with Bilqis in the narration.
key_terms.طَرْفَةِ عَيْنٍ: The blink of an eye, indicating extreme swiftness.
key_terms.عَرْشَ بِلْقِيسَ: The throne of Bilqis, which was brought to Sulayman through the divine secret mentioned in the hadith.
key_terms.عِلْمِ الْغَيْبِ: The knowledge of the unseen, belonging ultimately and uniquely to Allah.
key_terms.مُسْتَأْثِرٌ بِهِ: Exclusively reserved by Him, referring to what Allah alone retains.

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith about the seventy-three letters of Allah’s Greatest Name say about Asif and the Imams عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Greatest Name of Allah consists of seventy-three letters and that Asif possessed one of them, by which he performed the extraordinary act of bringing the throne of Bilqis to Sulayman. It further teaches that the Imams عليهم السلام possess seventy-two of these letters, while one remains exclusively with Allah in the knowledge of the unseen, indicating both their divinely granted knowledge and the absolute uniqueness of Allah's unseen knowledge.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Ali Bin Muhammad Al Nowfaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, the owner of the army, said, ‘

The Magnificent Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> are seventy three letters. One letter was with Asif (Bin Barkhiyya<sup>as</sup>, successor<sup>as</sup> of Suleyman<sup>as</sup>). So he<sup>as</sup> spoke with it, and the land was folded for him, in what was between him<sup>as</sup> and Saba (Sheba). So he<sup>as</sup> grabbed the throne of Bilquis until it came to be to Suleyman<sup>as</sup>. Then the earth extended back in less than the blink of an eye. And with us<sup>asws</sup>, from it, are seventy-two letters, and one letter is in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Accounting by it in the Knowledge of the unseen’.
en.sarwar: 3. al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ari from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Nawfali who has said that he heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) Sahib al-‘Askar say the following.

“The greatest name of Allah has seventy three letters. There was only one letter with Asif. He spoke with it and the land between him and the throne of the Queen of Sheba (Bilqis) sunk down as such that he took her throne and placed it before Solomon. The land then came to normal state within less than a blinking of an eye. There are seventy-two of those letters with us. One letter is with Allah which, He has kept it exclusively in the knowledge of the unseen.”
